abstract: Fanconi anemia (FA) is a heritable malformation, bone marrow failure and cancer predisposition syndrome that confers an exceptionally high risk of carcinomas arising in squamous epithelial lining the mouth, proximal esophagus, vulva and anus. The origin of these cancers is not understood, and no effective ways have been identified to prevent or delay these cancers. FA-associated carcinomas are challenging to treat: many are multi-focal, stage-advanced and not surgically curable at diagnosis, and most individuals with FA cannot be effectively treated with standard-of-care systemic therapies such as DNA cross-linking drugs and ionizing radiation due to their constitutional DNA damage hypersensitivity. We developed the Fanconi Anemia Cancer Cell Line Resource (FA-CCLR) of isogenic cell line pairs to address these clinical challenges and to foster new research on the origins, treatment, and prevention of FA-associated cancers. Ten new FANC isogenic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) cell line pairs were generated as part of this effort, 5 each from individuals with FA and 5 newly engineered from sporadic HNSCC cell lines. Newly engineered sporadic, isogenic cell lines were generated to provide directly comparable experimental material to use to identify HNSCC-associated cell and molecular phenotypes driven by germline or somatic loss of Fanconi pathway function and the subset that can be modified, complemented or suppressed. All of these FANC -isogenic cell line pairs are available to academic, non-profit and industry investigators via the ‘Fanconi Anemia Research Materials’ Resource and Repository at Oregon Health & Sciences University, Portland OR.
